title: Checksums, Versioning, and Error Detection
negative_results: a single-character corruption of the payload makes verify_vector() return False
a corrupted checksum tag fails verify()
a vector with no checksum separator is not verifiable and split_checksum() raises
a tag written under a different checksum version (cwck0) is rejected
a codec/version mismatch is detected by require_version() (ChecksumError)
a vector missing its codec=/v= version marker is refused
a single-digit error is detected by the Damm check digit
an adjacent transposition is detected by the Damm check digit

claims.statement: checksum()/verify() bind a CW vector with a version-tagged deterministic SHA-256 digest; a corrupted vector fails verification.

require_version() detects a codec-id or codec-version mismatch; a Damm check digit detects single-digit and adjacent-transposition typos. All utilities are deterministic (hashlib only, no wall-clock).
A passing checksum means a string is intact; it says nothing about what the string means or whether any source vector is geographic.

privacy_check: CLEAN - synthetic fixtures only, no private inputs
